body_markdown:
Hair loss is a common concern for men, and medications such as finasteride have become widely used to slow hair loss and encourage hair growth. For many people, the treatment can be effective. However, concerns about possible sexual and psychological side effects have continued to attract attention, particularly when symptoms appear to remain after treatment has been discontinued.


A recent case report involving a 26-year-old man has renewed discussion about the potential for persistent symptoms following finasteride use. According to a report published in the *Journal of Psychosexual Health* , the man experienced several sexual problems while taking the medication, and some symptoms continued for 19 months after he stopped using it.


## What Is Finasteride?


Finasteride is a prescription medicine used to treat male pattern hair loss as well as benign prostatic hyperplasia, a condition involving an enlarged prostate. The drug is one of the treatments approved for male pattern baldness.


The medication works by affecting the body's production of dihydrotestosterone, commonly known as DHT. DHT is a hormone involved in prostate growth and hair follicle changes associated with male pattern hair loss.


For men experiencing hair loss, finasteride can offer a medical option that may slow further loss or support regrowth. However, like other prescription medicines, it can also cause unwanted effects.


## A Young Man Reported Persistent Symptoms


The case highlighted in the recent report involved an unidentified 26-year-old man who was taking 1 milligram of finasteride for hair loss.


After approximately six months, he discontinued the medication because he had developed several troubling symptoms. These included reduced ejaculation, a substantial decrease in sexual pleasure and reduced sensation in the penis, medically described as genital hypesthesia.


The important part of the case was what happened afterward.


Rather than disappearing shortly after he stopped taking finasteride, the symptoms reportedly continued. The man eventually sought medical attention after experiencing the problems for 19 months following discontinuation.


This does not establish that every person who takes finasteride will experience persistent sexual symptoms. It is a report involving one individual, so it should be interpreted carefully. Nevertheless, the case contributes to an ongoing discussion about symptoms that some former users say can continue after treatment ends.


## Sexual Side Effects Have Been Reported


Sexual problems are among the side effects associated with finasteride. Reported concerns include erectile difficulties, changes in ejaculation and reductions in sexual desire or pleasure.


The case report adds another dimension because it involved a loss of genital sensation alongside changes in sexual function. The persistence of those symptoms was the reason the case attracted attention.


It is also important to distinguish between commonly reported adverse effects and the much more controversial question of long-lasting symptoms. A person experiencing a temporary side effect while taking a medicine is not necessarily experiencing the same condition as someone whose symptoms continue after stopping it.


## What Is Post-Finasteride Syndrome?


The term "post-finasteride syndrome," or PFS, is used to describe a collection of sexual, physical and psychological symptoms that are reported to continue after finasteride has been discontinued.


Reported symptoms can include reduced libido, erectile problems, genital sensory changes, fatigue, depression, anxiety, sleep problems, cognitive complaints and testicular discomfort.


The subject remains medically complex, and individual reports should not automatically be interpreted as proof that finasteride is responsible for every symptom that occurs after treatment. A case report can highlight a potential problem and encourage further research, but it cannot determine how frequently that problem occurs across the wider population.


That distinction matters when discussing medicines used by large numbers of people.


## Why Individual Cases Matter


Case reports are not the same as large clinical trials. A report describing one patient's experience cannot tell researchers how common a particular outcome is or prove that the medication directly caused every symptom.


However, individual cases can still be valuable. They may identify unusual or poorly understood experiences that deserve additional investigation.


In this situation, the reported persistence of sexual symptoms after discontinuation raises questions about why some individuals may experience longer-lasting problems while others do not. More research is needed to understand the mechanisms involved and determine the frequency and risk factors associated with persistent symptoms.


## Other Potential Concerns


The case report comes amid broader discussion surrounding finasteride and its possible adverse effects.


The source material notes that some men have reported erectile dysfunction, reduced sperm count and depression while taking the medication.


Psychological symptoms have also been reported in connection with concerns surrounding finasteride. These include anxiety, depression, fatigue, insomnia, reduced libido and cognitive complaints sometimes described as "brain fog." Suicidal thoughts have also been reported among some users.


Because these symptoms can have many possible causes, it is important not to assume that every occurrence is caused by finasteride. A healthcare professional can help assess symptoms and consider other potential explanations.


## What Should Men Do Before Taking Finasteride?


Anyone considering finasteride should discuss the treatment with a qualified healthcare professional before starting it.


A doctor can review your medical history, explain the potential benefits and risks, and discuss whether the medicine is appropriate for your particular situation. Patients should also be aware of the possible adverse effects listed for the medication and understand when they should seek medical advice.


Men already taking finasteride who develop new or concerning sexual, physical or psychological symptoms should speak with their healthcare provider. Stopping or changing prescription medication should be discussed with a medical professional rather than based solely on information found online.


The FDA has also previously warned about potential risks associated with compounded topical finasteride, according to the source material.


## The Bigger Picture


Finasteride remains an important treatment option for male pattern hair loss, and many men use it without experiencing the severe problems described in individual case reports. At the same time, reports of persistent symptoms deserve appropriate scientific attention.


The experience of the 26-year-old man described in the recent case report highlights why patients should be informed about possible adverse effects before beginning treatment. It also demonstrates the importance of further research into persistent symptoms following finasteride use.


For anyone considering treatment for hair loss, the best approach is an informed conversation with a healthcare professional. Hair loss can affect confidence and quality of life, but treatment decisions should take the full balance of potential benefits and risks into account.


### Sources


1. *Journal of Psychosexual Health* , case report concerning persistent sexual symptoms following finasteride use. The source article cited in the provided material is available through SAGE Publishing.
2. The New York Post report dated May 26, 2026.
3. FDA information concerning approved finasteride products and safety information referenced in the provided source.


### Disclaimer


This article is for general informational and educational purposes only. It is not medical advice, and it should not be used to diagnose, treat or prevent any medical condition. The case discussed involves an individual patient and does not establish that finasteride will cause persistent symptoms in all users. Anyone considering finasteride, experiencing side effects, or concerned about symptoms after stopping the medication should consult a qualified healthcare professional.
